svg.title: Empirical and testing logit distributions
svg.desc: Two panels, minority and majority. In each, a dashed Gaussian is the test logit density; to the right of the margin kappa* = 0.94 the solid curve and the simulated histogram agree with it. Everything the Gaussian puts below kappa is moved to a spike at kappa: 61% of the minority and 18% of the majority. The mass below zero, the test error, is 25.1% for the minority and 3.1% for the majority.
svg.text: Training logits are the test logits, truncated at the margin
Hard-margin SVM, n = 3000, d = 1200, ‖µ‖ = 1.75, π = 0.15. Bars: one run’s training margins. Curves: Theorem 2.1.
y · f(x) (distance past the boundary, signed)
y · f(x) (distance past the boundary, signed)
Dashed: the test-logit density N(ρ*‖µ‖ + yβ₀*, 1). Solid: its part above κ*, kept unchanged in training.
Shaded: test mass below κ*, moved onto the margin. β₀* = -0.60 puts the minority centre at 0.67, the majority’s at 1.86.
